title: AI-Assisted Smooth Counterexample to the Trautman Conjecture in CR Geometry & General Relativity
whyItMatters: Working with ChatGPT, geometer Sean N. Curry constructed a smooth strongly pseudoconvex counterexample refuting Andrzej Trautman’s CR-geometry conjecture tied to 4D null electromagnetic spacetimes.
summary: Posted to arXiv on September 2, 2026 (arXiv:2609.03198), mathematician Sean N. Curry—crediting ChatGPT with helping construct the argument—disproved Andrzej Trautman’s conjecture from general relativity and Cauchy–Riemann (CR) geometry. Trautman had conjectured that any smooth 3-dimensional CR manifold admitting a nowhere-zero closed section of its canonical bundle (equivalently a unimodular CR structure arising from null geodesic congruences in 4D Lorentzian spacetimes with null electromagnetic fields) must be locally embeddable in ℂ². Curry modified a nonembeddable strongly pseudoconvex CR structure via divergence-free vector fields so that the closed canonical form is preserved, proving that even arbitrarily small C¹ perturbations of S³ yield nonembeddable pseudo-Einstein CR structures and revealing a far richer family of 4D spacetime constructions than expected.
technicalHighlights: Refutes Trautman’s conjecture even in the strongly pseudoconvex (pseudo-Einstein) case and arbitrarily close in C¹ norm to the standard 3-sphere S³.
Shows Bryant’s geometric flow on unimodular CR 3-manifolds cannot always admit smooth two-sided local solutions.
Expands the known class of 3D CR manifolds generating 4D Lorentzian spacetimes with null electromagnetic fields.
caveats: Preliminary arXiv preprint awaiting independent journal refereeing; no formal Lean verification has been published.
